title: Certificates of Deposit: putting together the new term's rate and APY on a same-tier renewal
content:
## Scope

This rule states how the interest rate and the APY of the new term are put together when a Certificates of Deposit certificate renews into its own tier after the grace period, where rounding happens, and when no renewal is written at all.

## Rule

1. **Interest rate.** The new term's interest rate is the tier's published standard interest rate, plus the tier's jumbo bonus points when the jumbo bonus is earned, plus the tier's relationship bonus points when the relationship bonus is earned.
2. **One base, simple addition.** The two bonuses are added by simple addition to the same standard rate.
3. **Rounding once.** The sum is rounded half up to 2 decimal places once, at the end, and not after each addition.
4. **APY.** The new term's APY is the tier's published standard APY plus the same bonus points.
5. **No renewal written.** When the renewal has not yet fallen to be booked, when the maturity instruction is not automatic renewal, or when the renewal tier is a different tier, no renewal is written.

## Composition table

| Jumbo bonus earned | Relationship bonus earned | New term's interest rate before the final rounding |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Standard rate, plus jumbo points, plus relationship points |
| Yes | No | Standard rate, plus jumbo points |
| No | Yes | Standard rate, plus relationship points |
| No | No | Standard rate |

## Witness case for the rounding point (hypothetical three-decimal figures, not tier values)

A hypothetical standard rate of 3.784 percent, jumbo points of 0.103 and relationship points of 0.104, both bonuses earned.

- Correct: 3.784, plus 0.103, plus 0.104, gives 3.991, rounded once at the end to 3.99 percent.
- Wrong: rounding each figure first (3.78, 0.10, 0.10) and then adding gives 3.98 percent, which is not the rule.

## Worked example (hypothetical two-decimal figures)

Published standard rate 3.60 percent and standard APY 3.66 percent; jumbo points 0.10 earned; relationship bonus not earned.

- Interest rate: 3.60 plus 0.10 gives 3.70 percent.
- APY: 3.66 plus 0.10 gives 3.76 percent.

## Points of judgement

**Is the old term's rate a starting point for the new rate?**
No. The starting point is the tier's published standard interest rate, to which the earned bonus points are added.
